title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: Great compounding stories are often disguised inside messy legacy wrappers; the investor's edge lies in separating structural software economics from temporary chart extension.

web_blocks.html: Donnelley Financial Solutions, Inc. (NYSE: DFIN) leads in regulatory-compliance software and financial communications. As of the November 16, 2026 close, shares trade at $70.06 ($1.71 billion market cap; $1.81 billion enterprise value) [30]. DFIN spun off from R.R. Donnelley in October 2016 [3, 9]. Over the past decade, management shifted the business from physical printing to cloud-native Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) [9, 10]. In Q3 2026, Software Solutions crossed 51.5% of quarterly net sales [11, 23]. ActiveDisclosure (+24% to +29% YoY in 2026, >$100M TTM), Arc Suite, and Venue Virtual Data Rooms anchor this growth [11, 23]. On a strictly price-blind audit, DFIN earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL business quality verdict with PASS on all leading operational KPIs. It delivers 18.25% ROIC, 23.41% ROE, and a 31.3% FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA margin ($239.8M) [15, 30]. Free cash flow reached $107.8M in FY2025 (45.0% conversion), while net leverage sits near ~0.6x after an $82.8M pension settlement [15, 30, 34].

Yet fundamental quality and immediate entry timing diverge sharply at $70.06. DFIN surged +35.54% over one month and +45.47% over three months after earnings [30]. Shares now sit 16.75% above the 10-week EMA ($60.01) and 28.72% above the 50-day SMA ($54.43) [30]. RSI readings are overbought across 4H (71.59), 1D (76.82), and 1W (76.31) charts [30]. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 sits in a Correction regime with 6 distribution days and a 5.15% 10-year Treasury yield [30]. DFIN's options chain is also illiquid (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID) [30]. Against our $47.62 structural stop-loss and $92.00 12–18 month SOTP base target (4.25x Software EV/Sales + 5.0x CCM EV/EBITDA), chasing at $70.06 yields just 0.98:1 reward-to-risk. Waiting for an equity-only pullback into the $59.11–$64.55 support buy zone restores 1.62:1 asymmetry. Accordingly, DFIN receives a WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT verdict (CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT). We hold 0 shares today and keep 100% of earmarked tactical capital in CASH.

book_paragraphs: Welcome to Chapter Zero—the executive briefing for our ten-chapter institutional monograph on Donnelley Financial Solutions, ticker DFIN, as of the November 16, 2026 market close at $70.06 per share.

If you only remember one sentence from this entire book, make it this: Donnelley Financial Solutions is a genuinely high-return software transformation still wearing a cyclical print discount—but after a 45% three-month rally in a Correction market, your edge today is patience, not speed.

Let's frame the core thesis cleanly. When DFIN spun out of R.R. Donnelley on October 3, 2016, it looked like a sleepy financial printer destined to shrink alongside paper prospectuses. Its spin-off sibling, LSC Communications, doubled down on physical printing plants and went bankrupt in April 2020. DFIN's CEO, Daniel Leib, chose the opposite path: he used legacy print cash flows to pay down debt below one times EBITDA, settled $82.8 million of legacy pension obligations, and poured roughly $57 million a year into cloud-native regulatory software.

Ten years later, that bet has crossed the tipping point. In the third quarter of 2026, Software Solutions—led by ActiveDisclosure growing 24% to 29% year-over-year past a $100 million annual run-rate, Arc Suite for fund compliance, and a newly rebuilt Venue Virtual Data Room—crossed 51.5% of total revenue. Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA margins hit 31.3% in 2025, free cash flow conversion hit 45.0% ($107.8 million), and return on invested capital reached 18.25%. On a strictly price-blind fundamental audit, DFIN earns a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL quality verdict with PASS on all leading operational KPIs.

So why aren't we buying DFIN today at $70.06? Because valuation and technical timing have to agree before we risk capital. On Sum-of-the-Parts valuation—crediting Software Solutions at 4.25 times 2027 sales and valuing the shrinking legacy Compliance and Communications segment at a modest 5.0 times EBITDA—DFIN is worth roughly $92.00 per share over 12 to 18 months. That represents 31% upside from $70.06. However, DFIN's structural invalidation stop sits down at $47.62, just beneath its 200-day moving average.

Do the math: risking $22.44 per share to make $21.94 per share is a 0.98-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio. Worse still, DFIN is 16.75% above its 10-week EMA ($60.01) with overbought RSI readings above 71 to 76 across 4-hour, daily, and weekly charts, while the S&P 500 is in a Correction regime with 10-year Treasury yields at 5.15%. Our live options audit also confirms DFIN options are illiquid with bid-ask spreads over 14%, ruling out option spreads.

Therefore, our dual verdict is unambiguous: WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT). DFIN is currently NOT_HELD across our accounts, and we keep 100% of this tactical sleeve in Cash—passing for now on both our active shortlist compounder Microsoft (MSFT) and FinTech peer SS&C Technologies (SSNC)—while setting a firm alert at $64.55 to evaluate an equity-only entry inside the $59.11–$64.55 support buy zone, where reward-to-risk expands to 1.62-to-1.

book_subsections.title: 0A. The Five Numbers That Define DFIN Today
paragraphs: If you are listening on a commute and want the five anchor numbers that summarize Donnelley Financial Solutions as of November 16, 2026, lock these into memory. First, 51.5%: the share of Q3 2026 revenue now coming from Software Solutions, officially flipping DFIN from a financial printer into a software-majority franchise. Second, 18.25%: DFIN's trailing return on invested capital, higher than both Broadridge at 17.06% and Workiva at 9.46%.

Third, 8.06 times EV-to-EBITDA and 12.41 times forward earnings: the modest valuation multiples at $70.06 per share, reflecting lingering skepticism over legacy print and capital-markets cyclicality. Fourth, 76.82: DFIN's daily Relative Strength Index after a 45.5% three-month surge, flashing a clear warning against chasing. And fifth, $59.11 to $64.55: the institutional support buy zone where reward-to-risk toward our $92.00 base target resets to 1.62-to-1.

book_subsections.title: 0B. How the Dual-Edition Architecture Protects Your Capital
paragraphs: Notice how this monograph separates business quality from market timing. Too many investors fall in love with a great transformation story—like DFIN's decade-long pivot from paper to ActiveDisclosure and Arc Suite—and buy the stock at any price after a vertical earnings rally. Others look only at a 76.82 RSI chart and miss a multi-year compounder when it finally pulls back to support.

By grading business quality first in Chapters 1 through 6 without looking at the ticker's price, we know DFIN deserves a spot on our active watchlist. And by enforcing the Stage 2 support gate and 1.5-to-1 asymmetry rule in Chapters 7 through 9, we protect our capital from paying a FOMO tax in a Correction market. Set the $64.55 alert, keep your powder dry in Cash, and let the market come to you.

book_subsections.title: 0C. Why Patience Beats Prediction in a Correction Market
paragraphs: Nobody can predict whether DFIN's next 10% move is a continuation squeeze toward the $73.73 pivot or a sharp mean-reversion pullback toward the $60.01 10-week EMA. What we CAN control is our entry price, our position size, and our invalidation stop. When the S&P 500 is sitting below its 50-day moving average with six distribution days and 10-year Treasury yields at 5.15%, probability favors waiting for the market to offer you a discount rather than paying peak momentum prices.

If DFIN never pulls back to $59.11–$64.55 and runs away without us, that is completely fine—disciplined capital stays safe in cash or deploys into active Core Alpha setups like Microsoft (MSFT) that are already sitting inside their support zones. And if DFIN does cool off into our buy zone on light volume, we step in with a 1.62-to-1 asymmetry edge and a clear $92.00 destination.

Let's begin Chapter 1 at the beginning—on October 3, 2016, when R.R. Donnelley split itself into three public companies and set up one of the clearest corporate divergence experiments in modern financial services.
